questions.q: Which T-SQL clause is the Aggregate transformation's Group By operation directly analogous to?
options: GROUP BY
ORDER BY
WHERE
HAVING
questions.explain: The Aggregate transformation's Group By operation divides the dataset into groups, functioning like SQL's GROUP BY clause — but running entirely inside the data flow.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the Aggregate transformation's supported operations?
options: Sort
Sum
Count distinct
Maximum
questions.explain: Sort is a separate transformation entirely. The Aggregate transformation supports Group By, Sum, Average, Count, Count distinct, Minimum, and Maximum.

questions.q: If an Aggregate transformation's input has columns CountryRegion, City, and Population, and you group by CountryRegion while summing Population, what does the output contain?
options: Only CountryRegion and the summed Population — City is dropped entirely
All three original columns, unchanged, plus the sum
Only the summed Population column, with no grouping column at all
Every column duplicated once per group
questions.explain: The Aggregate transformation does not pass through untouched columns — it only outputs columns used for grouping or aggregation. Since City wasn't referenced, it doesn't appear in the output.

questions.q: Why is the Aggregate transformation described as 'asynchronous'?
options: It must consume the entire rowset before it can publish any output
It runs on a separate thread from the rest of the data flow at all times
It only works with asynchronous network connections
It cannot be used inside a synchronous control flow task
questions.explain: Unlike row-by-row transformations, the Aggregate transformation can't finalize a group's aggregation until it has seen every row in that group, so it consumes the whole rowset before producing output.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Keys or KeysScale property on a Group By operation?
options: To estimate how many groups the operation will produce, so the transformation can size its cache efficiently
To specify which column acts as the primary key for the output
To encrypt the grouping column's values
To limit the number of rows the transformation will accept as input
questions.explain: Keys (exact) and KeysScale (approximate) tell the Aggregate transformation roughly how many groups to expect from a Group By, letting it allocate memory more efficiently instead of guessing.
